why: Repairs scripts/ci/check_register_field_loss.py, a CI guard I shipped this morning in #11878 that has since been failing EVERY PR in the repository. Tier-1 by the canonical doc's own list: CI tooling only — no order path, no strategy config, no risk caps, no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no live-VM runtime file. It is NOT landing machinery: check_register_field_loss.py is absent from check_pr_landing.py's LANDING_MACHINERY (12 entries, read off origin/main by parsing the literal rather than by import), so R12 does not apply and `self` is honest. Two independent defects: (1) a removal declaration merged by another PR (mi279-u5-clear-digest-carrier.json, landed 10:54:46Z with #11915) was graded against every LATER diff as a PHANTOM, because load_removals() globbed the directory unconditionally; (2) the comparison base was origin/main's TIP rather than the merge-base, so any branch behind main reported every row main had gained since the fork as a loss that branch caused (measured on #11897: a row introduced four minutes after the branch's last merge). A third defect made both invisible: the self-test's last assertion was check('origin/main')['ok'] — a property of the live tree rather than of the checker — so a branch with a real finding printed 'the POLICY is broken'. The anti-silencer property is deliberately untouched: this SCOPES the declaration rather than dropping `phantom` from the verdict, so a declaration still has to be TRUE about the diff that carries it, and a row a branch genuinely removes is still a finding; both are pinned by their own self-test cases and both have plants. VERIFIED: 11/11 planted defects caught and the positive control quiet; each new never-collapsed state shown to fail when collapsed; and the fixed guard green on self-test AND live across three real branches that were red (#11897, #11900, #11923), against the unfixed guard measured red on the same trees. Does NOT touch .github/register-removals/mi279-u5-clear-digest-carrier.json — #11915's lane owns that file and it stays; deleting it by hand would have hidden the defect rather than fixed it.
